metadata.source: Computed from error_analysis_func_level_deepseek.json (n=1890, seed42 CLS × seed42 CWM)
metadata.note: Agreement breakdown derived from accuracy + oracle ensemble

cross_model_comparison.interpretation: DeepSeek shows nearly 2× higher complementarity (55.1% vs 31.2%) and 2× higher oracle gain (+4.6pp vs +2.1pp). This is driven by CWM's strong fail-bias in DeepSeek (fail recall 93.9% vs pass recall 78.2%), creating more differentiated error patterns between CLS and CWM. In Qwen3-4B, CLS and CWM learn more similar decision boundaries (95.4% agreement vs ~90% for DeepSeek).

per_label_asymmetry_deepseek.note: CWM is a conservative predictor (fail-biased). CLS is balanced. This asymmetry is the primary driver of their complementarity.
